images.caption: Avocado Egg Salad
images.description: Vitamins D3 and K2 are essential for directing calcium away from soft tissues (like blood vessels and kidneys) and into the bones. They cannot be absorbed effectively in a low-fat environment. Pairing soft-boiled or scrambled egg yolks with avocado ensures optimal absorption of Vitamin D3.

images.caption: Avocado Labneh Dip
images.description: While plant-based Vitamin K1 comes from greens, true Vitamin K2 (MK-4) is highly concentrated in the fat of fermented dairy from grass-fed cows. Blending the dense K2 fats of Labneh with the oleic acid in avocado creates a rich lipid matrix that ensures maximum absorption and that the calcium in the labneh goes to bones, not blood vessel walls.

images.caption: Mediterranean Salmon Avocado Salad
images.description: Carotenoids are fat-soluble antioxidants found in vibrant red, orange, and dark green plants. Because they require fat to be broken down and absorbed, pairing them with the rich monounsaturated fats in avocados can increase your body's carotenoid absorption by 3 to 15 times. • Kale, spinach, and romaine are packed with lutein, which protects the eyes and brain. A standard salad needs the fats in avocado to make these compounds bioavailable. Add pepitas and hemp hearts and the avocado increases the zinc and iron being split off and absorbed.
